patterns.comment: The reader declares a non-text scalar for these three. boot.js registers a tiddlerfield module for each: created and modified parse through parseDate, and color carries editType "color". A date reads as digits and a colour opens with #, which the block reader takes for a numbered list item — measured, colour alone accounts for 486 painted spans across 162 lines, every one of them wrong. The other two declared fields, tags and list, take the wikitext reading instead: see the rule below.
patterns.name: meta.tiddler.field.tiddlywiki5

patterns.comment: A value in the filter language, not in wikitext. TiddlyWiki declares no field type for these, so the set stands as a ruling rather than a harvest, and the reason is measurable: a filter variable reads <count> and <targetTiddler>, which the wikitext reader takes for an HTML tag. Measured across TiddlyWiki’s own tiddlers, condition alone paints 429 spans that name nothing.
patterns.name: meta.tiddler.field.tiddlywiki5

patterns.comment: Base-64 image bytes. A blob of base-64 carries [[ and // by accident of the alphabet, and the reader paints 1622 wikilink spans and 429 italics across ten fields. Bytes name no tiddler.
patterns.name: meta.tiddler.field.tiddlywiki5

patterns.comment:
Every other header field takes the wikitext reading.

The reading follows the readers rather than a taste for colour. A header value carries a tiddler name far more often than it carries anything else, and the two readers spell a tiddler name the same way: boot.js:406 parses a title list with parseStringArray, whose bracketed member survives the round trip through stringifyList, and filters.js:24 parses [[Some Title]] as a run whose empty operator defaults to title. The enlist operator joins them outright, taking a string-array operand inside a filter. So the brackets in tags and list mark a quoted title under BOTH readers, and the mark carries the colour.

Measured over TiddlyWiki’s 7012 .tid and .meta files: tags paints 15317 spans and not one falls outside the tiddler-name family; across 3122 bracketed members none carries a pipe, so the one shape that would part a quoted title from a pretty link stands empty. Opening every field but the ruled sets above reads 11443 lines rightly and 19 wrongly.

A value opens mid-line inside a capture, so the block rules anchored on ^ stand aside and the inline ones reach the value as a reader meets it. A capture confines to its own span, so an unclosed construct cannot swallow the field line beneath it — ten broken values probed, ten boundaries held.
patterns.name: meta.tiddler.field.tiddlywiki5

patterns.comment: A control character alone breaks a field name; TW5 v5.2.x admits every other character in one.
patterns.name: invalid.illegal.field.name.tiddlywiki5

dictionary-entry.comment:
One entry of a tiddler dictionary: a key, a colon, and a value TiddlyWiki renders as wikitext.

A dictionary key names no tiddler field, so the allow-list above — text, caption, description — reads nothing here: a dictionary carrying an entry called `caption` carries a key of that name and not a caption. Every value takes the wikitext reading instead, which the ground supports: of 2863 entries across TiddlyWiki’s own 28 dictionaries, 958 carry a wikitext construct, most of them a `<<colour ...>>` call in a palette.

The scopes come from the field reading above rather than from names of their own. An entry carries a key and a value, the reading matches, and a scope of its own would ask the corpus for ground that says nothing new.
dictionary-entry.name: meta.tiddler.field.tiddlywiki5
